_about: Built by research-hub tools/build_s87_money.py from external sources (data/s87/SOURCES.md). Descriptive history; no simulation figure.

events.label: Coinage Act: dollar defined in silver and gold, 15 to 1
events.source: 1 Stat. 246, sec. 11 ("the proportional value of gold to silver ... shall be as fifteen to one")

events.label: Coinage Act of 1834: gold coin made lighter (about 16 to 1)
Coinage Act of 1873: the standard silver dollar dropped
events.source: 17 Stat. 424, sec. 15 (silver coins listed: trade dollar, half, quarter, dime)

events.label: Gold Standard Act: gold the single standard
events.source: 31 Stat. 45 (approved March 14, 1900): the dollar of 25.8 grains of gold nine-tenths fine "shall be the standard unit of value"

events.label: Executive Order 6102: private gold delivered to the Federal Reserve by May 1
events.source: Executive Order 6102, April 5, 1933 (American Presidency Project text)

events.label: Gold Reserve Act (Jan 30) and Proclamation 2072 (Jan 31): $35 an ounce
events.source: 48 Stat. 337; Proclamation 2072 fixes the gold dollar at 15 5/21 grains nine-tenths fine, which is $35.00 per fine ounce

events.label: Coinage Act of 1965: silver taken out of dimes and quarters
Silver certificates no longer redeemable in silver
events.source: 81 Stat. 77 (Public Law 90-29, June 24, 1967), sec. 2: exchangeable for silver bullion for one year after enactment

events.label: Gold window closed: dollar's convertibility into gold suspended
events.source: President Nixon's address of August 15, 1971 (American Presidency Project text)

events.label: Private gold ownership legal again
events.source: 88 Stat. 445 (Public Law 93-373, approved August 14, 1974): effective December 31, 1974, or earlier

college.label: A year of college: tuition, fees, room and board (NCES, all institutions)
college.note: Academic year starting in the autumn of the year shown

tuition.label: A year of college: tuition and required fees only (NCES)

minwage.label: A week at the federal minimum wage
